Subject: MSA redlines — injunctive relief + seat question

Marcus — thanks for the redlines. Two quick but important items from our GC team: 1) We cannot accept a clause that effectively forces all injunctions into arbitration without an emergency carveout; Aurora needs an express right to seek injunctive or provisional relief in state or federal court where necessary to protect PHI and patient safety. 2) If you insist on arbitration for the main dispute resolution path, we need clarity on forum (seat) for interim relief and how that interacts with any arbitration stay.

Can your legal team propose language that: (a) preserves our ability to seek emergency injunctive relief in court, (b) states whether Redwood will consent to provisional measures in a nominated seat, and (c) identifies the default seat if arbitration is chosen?

Kara

From: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Kara Simmons <legal@aurorahealth.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed compromise language — emergency relief carveout + seat fallback

Kara / Marcus — draft language below that we believe balances Aurora's need for immediate injunctive relief and Redwood's operational need for predictability. Please review and let us know if any edits are required.

Proposed redline (MSA §14 Dispute Resolution):
"Notwithstanding any agreement to arbitrate disputes between the Parties, either Party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to protect its confidential information, trade secrets, or to prevent irreparable harm to patient safety or PHI. The Parties agree that, absent an emergency showing, an application for provisional measures shall be brought in the seat of arbitration (New York, NY) and the arbitrator may decide whether to stay any court proceedings. For clarity, seeking provisional relief in court shall not constitute a waiver of rights to compel arbitration of the underlying dispute."

Notes: 1) We nominate New York as the default seat for provisional measures to keep a single predictable forum. 2) We included explicit PHI/patient-safety language to address your point. 3) This preserves arbitration for the merits and permits emergency court filings narrowly.

Attachments: redline PDF and a one-page matrix with seat pros/cons.

Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Olga — appreciate the fast turnaround and the PHI callout. Two questions from Aurora GC: (1) Will Redwood accept 'no requirement to show irreparable harm' language for expedited temporary relief in cases involving PHI, or do you want the standard threshold? We prefer a lower evidentiary bar for immediate limited relief. (2) If the default seat is New York, will Redwood confirm that Aurora can nonetheless seek provisional relief in local court where the harm occurs (e.g., CA state or federal court) pending transfer/coordination with NY? We need operational certainty for emergency filings.

If you can confirm those two points we can move this into an internal sign-off this week.

Kara

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed compromise language — emergency relief carveout + seat fallback

Kara — quick reply from our side: (1) We cannot broadly accept a 'no requirement to show irreparable harm' standard; that is too expansive. However, we will accept a tailored evidentiary relaxation limited to filings that demonstrably concern PHI or imminent patient safety risks — i.e., a short list of triggers. (2) Aurora may file in a local court for provisional measures where the harm occurs. Our proposal: allow local emergency filings, but require prompt notice to Redwood and an explanation; parties will cooperate to transfer or seek stay to the nominated seat (NY) within 7 calendar days unless a court orders otherwise.

Operational ask: Marcus/aditya — can your team confirm whether a 7-day coordination window is workable from a sales/ops perspective (timing for notices, who receives them, contact points)? Also, if Aurora wants court filings in CA, we may need a quick escalation path for our legal ops team to collect log/audit evidence.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Legal Ops (Redwood)
